reminders.text: Pause. This is an impulse to escape a feeling.
This is the 'I don’t care anymore' moment. It will pass.
You are trying to reward a feeling—not feed hunger.
If you are physically hungry, eating is the correct action.
You are in a stressful social situation right now. Focus on safety first.
What happened hurt you. Food won’t resolve it, only delay it.
Stopping now is still stopping. You are not trapped.

actions.text: Delay ordering food for 10 minutes. Do nothing else.
Do not continue automatically. Put the food down for 60 seconds.
Sit still and breathe slowly for 2 minutes before deciding anything.
Change environment immediately (stand up, leave room).
If you still want it after 10 minutes, reassess—not react.
Eat a real, simple meal now (not snack looping).
If being bullied: prioritize getting away or ending exposure.
Write down what happened instead of reacting with food.

meals.text: Ham + cheese + bread (simple plate, not grazing)

tips.text: Your binges are shutdown responses, not food decisions.
The 'I don’t care anymore' feeling is temporary emotional collapse.
Bullying creates threat response—your brain seeks escape behaviors.
After bullying, your mind replays events—food becomes distraction, not solution.
Impulse eating feels urgent but peaks and fades quickly.
Eating regularly reduces emotional intensity, but does not solve triggers alone.
You are not stuck in the binge—you are inside a moment of overwhelm.

options: If you still want food, choose ONE item only
Write your current feeling before ordering
Do a non-food reward first (walk, shower, music)
If ordering, choose single-portion food only

impulse_order: This urge will peak and fall.
binge_shutdown: You are in a stress response.

impulse_order: You don’t need to act now.
It will weaken if you wait.
